UPDATE 6/24/17:

In early May 2017, I was washing a load of laundry in this washing machine, switched it to the "drain" function, and walked away to let the water drain into my tub, as usual. When I returned to check on it, there was water all over my floor. The drain hose had cracked, causing a huge puddle. I promptly turned the machine off, unscrewed the back, and looked to see if the hose was easily replaceable. It didn't look to be, so I emailed the manufacturer Della through its own website and then the seller (One Big Outlet) through Amazon, asking for a replacement or ideally a refund. I put in two emails to both Della and One Big Outlet, and neither responded over the course of weeks. Della's website literally has no phone number listed, and a Google search yielded no results. One Big Outlet had a phone number that I tried twice, but both times, it went to voicemail and told me I couldn't leave a voicemail because the voicemail box was full. I had purchased Assurant coverage for this, but was told they couldn't help me because it only covered electrical and mechanical damage, not physical damage. It was only after three very long calls to Amazon that Amazon itself agreed to refund me. This was just resolved last week after at least a month of trying for this refund. At the time when the machine broke, I had had it for less than a year and am only one person using it gently. This should not have happened, but it did, so either the manufacturer or sell

Well. Overall I am extremely satisfied with this purchase. I spent many months researching this product and read dozens if not hundreds of reviews. I came to the conclusion that all of these portable twin tub washers provide the same function and produce the same results. I live in a micro apartment (less than 225 sq. ft.) so my primary concerns were fitting this into my space and avoiding laundromats. I was fully aware of the various complaints made by other reviewers and went into this purchase with eyes wide open.

First. Delivery was in 2 business days.

Second. Package arrived in good condition and washer was well packed inside.

Third. On initial inspection, item appeared new and was undamaged in any way.

Fourth. I wanted to plug it in and check for operation before trying to do a load of wash.

Fifth (and here's why only 4 stars). Sure enough, I plugged it in, turned on the wash-side timer and heard the motor turning, but the agitator wasn't moving. I stopped the was timer and turned on the spin timer. That worked fine. I'm not AT ALL mechanically inclined, but I figured that since I could hear the wash motor turning but the agitator was not, that either there was a loose, missing, broken or unconnected belt. So I tipped the washer over, located the access panel on the bottom rear, removed it and looked inside. There it was. Nothing major but expect a few drops on the floor. Considering this Della is almost $100 less than the 19lb Panda, it's a small hassle.

Filling the wash tub takes forever. If you have a 5 gallon bucket, filling it in the shower and then dumping it into the washer would be much faster. I just do it the intended way and multitask while it's filling.

So I find small loads are easier. You will likely want to wash. Rinse. Rinse. Spin. Or even wash wash rinse rinse spin. On spinning: the timer goes up to 5 mins. Very few things need 5 mins. People bring up not over loading or loading perfect. Don't worry. 1. Everything is plastic. 2. You can reset the stuff 3. I encourage you to reset.
I fill it 3/4 say 3 towels. I set to 35 seconds give or take. Then stop. Reset. Then 30 seconds to 1 min. 2 if it's cotton or other dense non synthetic type.

And if you buy a tiny dryer too. Get stuff super dry. Even half hang dry and get some wool dryer balls. I'm sure all the people bitching about 2 hours for a towel put it in soaking wet. Tbh. I'm buying a little dryer mostly for delinting ...and times I forget to plan.

I don't have the space for a full-sized washer and dryer, and overall this washer has been more convenient for me than going out to a laundromat.

So all the reviews I read about this machine were accurate. You need to put a little work into it for it to be just perfect.
What you will need:
Garden Hose
Hose connecting Adapter
Clamp Rings
Eye Hoods
Craft Wire

Working with what you have:
The hose is 2 small and you need an adapter. I found a simple solution by going to home depot and getting a clear hose to attach to the hose. Before inserting the hose I inserted a plastic connector into the open end of the washing machine hose.
This allowed the hose to remain in place in the clear hose.
I then used clamp rings to make sure it would not come out and hold it together.
I have made this portable mini washing machine into a non-movable one by putting the hose to drain in the sink.
I attached eye hooks to the wall and used craft wire to wrap around the hose and threaded it through the hooks.
The hose for intake is also too small.
Easy fix for that situation as well.
I took a garden hose found an adapter for my kitchen sink ( don't drink tap water anyway so removed tap filter to place adapter)
Now when I want to use the machine I only have to connect the hose and fill the tub with hot or cold water depending on what I'm washing.

The machine itself is amazing and cleans stuff really well. I had to use the reviews here and YouTube to figure out how to work it because my instructions had been translated from Italian and never really corrected. The pictures were pretty unhelpful too so I'll share what I learned:

Store this close to the kitchen sink for easier access. The cord is short so invest in an extension cord of some sort. You will absolutely need to fill this from a sink so be prepared for that. It's also bigger than you think probably and weighs 9kg empty. I'm disabled and it's difficult for me to carry so I have to scoot it everywhere so keep the size and weight in mind. I'm about 6 foot and this comes up to my stomach and is about as wide abouts two of me. So it's about the size of a full machine.

You have to fill it from the back. The detached hose connects to one of two of the small circular bits in the back. The one for the washer is just that, for the rinse and wash cycles. The one for the dryer I'm told helps get suds out of clothes but I have no idea how that would drain to eventually dry clothes so I don't use it. Instead I keep using rinse cycles until the clothes are totally clean.

There's a small metal ring that comes with this meant to clamp the larger end of the fill hose to the sink faucet. If yours is anything like mine, good luck getting any of that to work. You'll have to invest in an adapter. Take the hose with you to a real physical store so yo

This washer is a lot bigger than I expected so the set up that I have is a bit awkward (it's in my already-very-tiny-bathroom). Other than that, it washes well and the spinner wrings out the water to where my clothes are nearly dry (I would say about 75-80% dry). This does have a built in pump to help drain the water out and it's pretty fast. I do still use my apartment complex's laundry room for the dryer, but at least I don't have to dry a load at such high heat for a full hour; 30-45mins seems to be adequate depending what I'm drying.

What I don't like is that the inlet hoses are too short for the set up that I was hoping to create and the plastic used to build the wash basin doesn't feel like it can hold a full 9kg (or 19 lbs) of laundry. Therefore, I stick with doing medium size loads.

Other than that, I recommend this to anyone who lives in an apartment or condo who's looking for an alternative to a laundromat or are tired of having to wait their turn for a machine in their community laundry room.

The panda equivalent is double the price, but it has better quality motors built in. These machines are very simple and rely on 2 motors. Della needs to invest in high quality motor components. Once the motor issue is addressed it will be a wonderful product. It is big capacity and can handle a whole set of queen size sheets. But unfortunately, I have to return it. I will invest and get the big capacity Panda machine. My old trusty twin tub that I have had for decades has finally passed on, and I can no longer find any technician to service it, so with a lot of heart ache I will recycle the machine (it's a Hoovermatic, that was passed on to me by my Grand Mother).

It’s been six months since I bought my Della and I’ve loved it for saving me money. I opted to move to an apartment much cheaper than my previous and it was the first time I found myself without a washer and dryer. So for entire first month, I washed panties by hand in kitchen sink and bought new outfits whenever my clothes became unwearable. So.... there's nothing negative I can say about this portable washing machine. It's 1000x better than what I've been doing, and it washes far more than just undergarments.

It's super easy to hook up and get started. The instructions suck and make it seem difficult but YouTube it and watch a video. It requires minimal preparation.

The hoses are flimsy and cheap and I've seen other people getting crafty with garden hoses and such but it's not necessary. The hose included works. You just need a kitchen or bathroom sink faucet that is narrow. The opening should be an inch in diameter, roughly.

The main complaint is that it takes forever to fill it up with water (and you have to do it twice for one load--soapy water and clean water). But you can get a fairly large load of laundry done in one cycle. I did the first load today (as soon as I received it) and I did 2 skirts, 2 pants, 4 shirts, a few pairs of PJs, panties, and socks in one load (about 2 armfuls of clothing).

The spinner dries it fairly well. It's still damp when you remove the material but it's not dripping or anything. I stick it on a laundry rack and it's dry overnight.

Honestly, it's convenient and easy

Prior to this, I had the Panda XPB45 larger model, it's almost the same size as this Della. I had the Panda for 4 years, and it worked really well, except with time, all the electrical connectors starting failing, so I had to turn the dials several times before it would "take". Eventually, one of the dials failed completely, so it had to be discarded. I've bought this Della to replace it.

I've taken a close look, and it seems pretty much the same design as the Panda, with few differences. So far, I've only used it a handful of times, and I like it overall. The agitation is strong, and it's quite capacious. So far so good. The one DEFINITE negative compared to the Panda is that the pump is SUPER WEAK. It struggles to pump out the water, with barely a trickle, and most of the time it takes about a minute before it manages to work up any water at all. For all intents and purposes it's almost like a gravity outflow.

Now, I have the drain hose outlet about the height of the top of the machine, so it would probably do better if it was lower, but then I had the Panda at the same height, and the pump worked just fine.

The real test will be how long this machine lasts - my Panda lasted a solid 4 years, and I'd be happy if this Della did so too, but that remains to be seen.

We bought this little washer for our motor home. I used it on our front porch at home before we hit the road. For the price and the job it can't be beat! I was very satisfied with the washing process. It wrings out the clothes beyond amazing! I placed it in front of our shower in the bathroom and used the shower sprayer to fill it up. I could've done the same thing at the kitchen sink but draining just seemed easier in the shower to me. You can wash way more than you can spin at one time. After washing I let it spin it's cycle then put more into the spin side. It spins so much out the clothes that they are just damp. I washed jeans, towels, underwear, everything I would wash at home except our sheets. I will eventually wash sheets in this as well. You do have to drain and refill the washer between cycles. I used Tide in the wash cycle and added Downy to the rinse cycle. I highly recommend buying a drying rack before you wash your clothes. We had clothes hanging all over the motor home because I forgot to get one ahead of time. Powerful little washer with BIG results in my opinion! Very happy customer!
